v.why: Adding the input-output residual is most valuable when it is absent (exps 71,75,78 gave +15-20 on IN16).
Filling a missing input-output edge gives large gains (exps 11,15,18) versus replacing an existing op.
Replacing the identity shortcut with a conv removes the residual path and was negative in exps 12,16,19.
With edge 1 also absent, removing edge 0 cuts input to nodes 1 and 2, causing 10-20 point drops (exps 25-27).
When node 1 is dead, the node2->output path carries all computation, so a conv there helps a lot (exps 8-10).
Replacing a parameter-free pool on the only path into node 1 with a conv consistently helped (exps 84,87,90).
Skip already passes useful features to node 1, so swapping it for a 1x1 conv gains little (exps 82,86,89).
Removing a 3x3 conv loses more capacity than removing skip or pool (exp 21 vs 22,23).
Upgrading skip to a 3x3 conv on node1->output was consistently positive across datasets (exps 42,46,49).
Replacing avg pooling on input->node2 with a 3x3 conv gave consistently large gains (exps 54,57,60).

raw:
Ten hypotheses, chosen where the 100 experiments show a consistent conditional pattern that also fits how NAS-Bench-201 cells behave:

1. **Edge 3 → skip_connect helps much more when edge 3 is none.** Experiments 71, 75 and 78 gained +15 to +20 points on IN16. Adding the input→output residual matters most when it is missing.
2. **Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 3 is none.** Experiments 11, 15 and 18 were large gains, mostly from reconnecting the input to the output.
3. **Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 helps less when edge 3 is skip_connect.** Experiments 12, 16 and 19 were all negative. Losing the identity shortcut hurts.
4. **Edge 0 → none hurts much more when edge 1 is none.** Experiments 25–27 lost 10–20 points. With edge 1 also absent, nodes 1 and 2 get no input.
5. **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 0 is none.** Experiments 8–10 gained +8 to +10 on IN16. With node 1 dead, the node 2→3 path carries all the computation.
6. **Edge 0 → nor_conv_1x1 helps more when edge 0 is avg_pool_3x3.** Experiments 84, 87 and 90 all gained. A parameter-free pool on the only path into node 1 is weak.
7. **Edge 0 → nor_conv_1x1 helps less when edge 0 is skip_connect.** Experiments 82, 86 and 89 were weakest. Skip already feeds node 1 well.
8. **Edge 0 → none hurts more when edge 0 is nor_conv_3x3.** Experiments 21 and 24 lost more than 22 and 23. Removing a conv costs more than removing skip or pool.
9. **Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 4 is skip_connect.** Experiments 42, 46 and 49 were consistently positive.
10. **Edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 1 is avg_pool_3x3.** Experiments 54, 57 and 60 were consistently large gains.
